Hey everyone.

(INTRO YADDA-YADDA. Skip if you're bored)
I'm new to the group: this is my first post and I'll propably stick to
keeping a low profile and only dropping by once in a while to check in
on the progress and development of V:TES.
I've been a player with a smaller local playgroup for quite some time
(which my nickname makes quite obvious) however we don't have the most
up to date rulebook around here as finding a shop that stocks newer
V:TES cards is hard. That's why the question might be a bit stupid.
I also tried searching but did not come up with any satisfying
results/answers.

(RULES QUESTION)
What kind of Cross-Table Actions/Reactions are allowed?

I know that without special cards BLEED (d) Actions are always
directed at your prey. A few cards are the exception to this rule.

I know that undirected actions (equip, political) can only be blocked
by your prey and predator (in that order). Of course, a few cards
(eagle's sight) allow you to circumvent this restriction.

But what I'm unsure about are (d) Actions such as regular Rushes,
Burning the Mob Connections, Stealing the Rack, Emptying a
Powerbase...

Someone here willing to help?

Thanks in advance.

> I've been a player with a smaller local playgroup for quite some time

> up to date rulebook around here as finding a shop that stocks newer
> V:TES cards is hard. That's why the question might be a bit stupid.
> I also tried searching but did not come up with any satisfying
> results/answers.
>
> (RULES QUESTION)
> What kind of Cross-Table Actions/Reactions are allowed?
>
> I know that without special cards BLEED (d) Actions are always
> directed at your prey. A few cards are the exception to this rule.
>

You can only direct bleed actions at your prey. Explicit card text (Night
Moves, Kindred Spirits) is needed to circumvent this.

> I know that undirected actions (equip, political) can only be blocked
> by your prey and predator (in that order). Of course, a few cards
> (eagle's sight) allow you to circumvent this restriction.
>

FYI, blocking with Eagle's Sight also allows you to block actions directed
at another player.

> But what I'm unsure about are (d) Actions such as regular Rushes,
> Burning the Mob Connections, Stealing the Rack, Emptying a
> Powerbase...
>

If it is not a bleed action, then D actions may be driected at any viable
target, regardless of target's controller, within the limits set by the card
(cf. Harass, Ambush, etc.)

D actions provided by a card in play may be taken by anyone, unless card
text limits this. So yes, you can steal the Rack cross-table (its an action
directed at the Rack's current controller).

Regards
DaveZ
Atom Weaver
